one_liner: Course-project CUDA 2-D R2C FFT for binary (0/1) sparse matrices; beats dense cuFFT on mid-size non-power-of-2 inputs.
what_it_does: Computes the full 2-D real-to-complex FFT (rows x (cols/2+1) half-spectrum, single precision) of a sparse matrix whose nonzeros are all treated as 1, without ever building the dense rows x cols grid. It is a benchmark executable (cuSpFFT <matrix.mtx> [flags]) that reads Matrix Market files, expands symmetric storage, binarizes values, and runs dense cuFFT, optional SpFFT and its own variants side by side; the C++ entry points (e.g. sparse_fft_csc_bluestein_cufft_smooth(const COOMatrix&, int u_tile)) return a device pointer the caller must free, so library use means lifting functions out of the tree.
how_it_is_fast: Pass 1 walks a compact CSC (empty columns dropped, no values array, uint16_t indices when rows and cols are at most 65,536) and computes the row-direction DFT directly from the nonzeros, one (output-row tile, column) block per CUDA block with no atomics. The column-direction DFT of arbitrary width is done with Bluestein's chirp-z convolution at a smooth length (3-smooth for the custom radix-2/3/fused-9 Stockham FFT, 7-smooth for the cuFFT-backed variant) instead of padding to a power of two. Output rows are processed in tiles of 128, so scratch memory is 2 x tile x fft_len complex values rather than a dense input plus cuFFT workspace, which is where the ~10x memory saving comes from.
when_to_use: 2-D FFT of graph adjacency or other 0/1 sparsity patterns with a few thousand to ~65k rows, densities around 0.1-0.4%, and a non-power-of-2 width (benzene 8,219^2: 9.60 ms vs 23.64 ms dense cuFFT on an RTX 4090).
Inputs where dense cuFFT cannot plan or fit in device memory (pct20stif 52,329^2: dense plan creation failed and SpFFT ran out of memory; the cuFFT-backed sparse variant finished in 893 ms).
Memory-constrained GPUs: the sparse variants used 310-317 MB vs 3,305 MB for dense cuFFT on benzene; the experimental streaming flag ran pct20stif at about 474 MB.
As a worked example of Bluestein-at-smooth-length plus tiled sparse front ends on CUDA (README documents factorizations, Nsight profiles and ablations).
when_not_to_use: Power-of-2 widths: delaunay_n14 (16,384^2) took 68.56 ms (cuFFT-backed) and 304.76 ms (custom) vs 7.81 ms for dense cuFFT, because Bluestein doubles the transform length and the pipeline runs five passes.
Small matrices: on sstmodel (3,345^2) dense cuFFT took 0.85 ms vs 1.39 ms and 3.62 ms for the sparse variants.
Weighted (non-binary) sparse data: values are discarded on read, so the output is the FFT of the sparsity pattern, not of the matrix.

Matrices with more than 65,536 rows: the pass-1 phase index is computed as ((uint32_t)u * (uint32_t)r) % rows, which wraps once rows^2 exceeds 2^32 and would give wrong twiddles for non-power-of-2 row counts (not tested by the repo, whose largest case has 52,329 rows).
Any shipped product: there is no licence file, so the code is reference-only; it is a CSC 766 course submission with 13 commits and no releases.

integration.form: source-drop (single CMake executable; no installable library target)
integration.dependencies: CUDA Toolkit 12.x with cuFFT, cuBLAS, cuSPARSE and NVTX; optional SpFFT (CUDA, single precision) and FFTW3 single precision for baselines and correctness checks
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.20+, C++17 host compiler, nvcc from CUDA 12.x (tested with 12.5.82); CMake falls back to sm_80 when no architecture is given
integration.platforms: Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (tested on RTX 4090, compute capability 8.9)
integration.thread_safety: not documented (functions launch on the default stream and allocate per call)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — produces the same R2C half-spectrum as cufftExecR2C for 0/1 inputs, but takes a COO matrix instead of a dense array, pads the output row stride to a multiple of 4 complex values, and has no plan/exec API

gotchas: Reported times are CUDA-event timings of the transform loop only: host COO-to-CSC conversion, index uploads and the Bluestein kernel precompute are outside the timed region, as are dense densification and cufftPlan2d for the baseline.

Accuracy is lower than dense cuFFT: max_abs error vs the FFTW single-precision reference on benzene is 2.0e-01 for the custom FFT path and 6.3e-02 for the cuFFT-backed path vs 4.7e-02 for dense cuFFT (twiddles use the fast __sincosf intrinsic).
The reported non-streaming variants keep the full output on the device (about 11 GB for pct20stif); only the experimental --csc-stockham-cufft-stream path bounds memory by tile size.
Default --csc-tile is 1024 while the reported runs use 128, and --repeat defaults to a single run with no warm-up; pass --csc-tile 128 --repeat 10 to match the README tables.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The GPU FFT siblings (VkFFT, tcFFT, TurboFFT) are dense uniform FFTs and win whenever the dense grid fits and the width is FFT-friendly; FINUFFT/cuFINUFFT handles nonuniform points and MPSFT targets spectra with few large coefficients. Pick cuSpFFT only to study or adapt an input-sparse, binary-valued 2-D transform whose dense cuFFT plan is too large or whose width is awkward (large prime factors), keeping in mind it cannot be copied without a licence.
verified_claims_summary: On one RTX 4090 (CUDA 12.5.82, Release, sm_89), median of 10 runs after a warm-up, the cuFFT-backed sparse variant ran benzene (8,219^2, 0.36% dense) in 9.60 ms and the fully custom one in 14.65 ms vs 23.64 ms for dense cuFFT R2C (2.46x and 1.61x), with about one tenth of the device memory; it loses on small and power-of-2 matrices, and SpFFT (~32 ms, single run) was slower than dense.
status_note: Finished course project (final submission April 2026, last commit a .gitignore change on 2026-05-24) with no licence, so treat it as reference material rather than a dependency.
